investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, meaning the peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are fully consumed. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 capacity-constrained nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 128–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: The eval for check published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was last generated 717 minutes ago, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot itself is structurally valid and was produced by github-actions (source field confirms this), but it is approximately 11 hours and 57 minutes old at eval time, indicating the scheduled or triggered workflow either did not fire, was skipped, queued and timed out, or failed to publish the updated file to the GitHub Pages endpoint. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, meaning the peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are fully consumed. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 capacity-constrained nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 128–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
